novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism/measurement route rather than merely a new setting: it asks whether features "causally deactivate" under mutations that "physically break a mechanism" while remaining stable under conservation-matched, mechanism-preserving mutations, with a physics-based dose response. The closest prior work is InterPLM (2024), the 2025 PNAS sparse-autoencoder study, and "From Mechanistic Interpretability to Mechanistic Biology" (2025), which identify or annotate PLM features, while METL (Nature Methods, 2025) incorporates biophysical training signals but does not test whether features learned by an evolutionary PLM track physical mechanisms; searches for "protein language model mechanistic interpretability counterfactual mutation physical mechanism," "ESM-2 SAE causal intervention biophysics," and "protein language model evolutionary correlation mutational test" found no essentially equivalent study. The step from those works to this claim requires a new core relationship—a physics-grounded causal criterion separating evolutionary correlation from mechanism—rather than a direct transfer or routine object substitution, supporting a high-but-within-framework score of 7 rather than a paradigm-level 9–10.
